Resolves #19934

Calling the method on the table body, as the ticket suggests, only moves the error: `table.body.createViewData()` takes no arguments and builds rows from the body's store (`store.getCount()`). These tables have no store, so the page then threw `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getCount')`. `MainContainer3.mjs` already made that call and would fail the same way, but the page never got that far.

So the example now uses the table the current way:
- `examples/tablePerformance/fields.mjs` (new): the row fields, `id` plus `columnN` and `columnNstyle` for the ten columns, so the existing `columnDefaults.renderer` still finds the background color on the record.
- Each of the three tables gets `store: {model: {fields}}`.
- `Viewport#createRandomData()` gives every row an `id` (the store's key).
- `updateTableViewData()` loads the rows with `table.store.data = inputData` in all three containers. "Refresh 100x" goes through the same method.

Checked in headless Chromium (Playwright 1.64.1) against `webpack serve`, without network:

| | `dev` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| table errors | `table.createViewData is not a function` | none |
| DOM nodes | 1 | 2079 |
| rows per table (incl. header) | – | 21, 51, 101 |

Both runs also log `Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON` from an unrelated request in my offline setup.

Note: I used Claude Code while working on this.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: Merge-safe repair for `#19934` (`examples/tablePerformance`). The originating ticket suggested changing `table.createViewData(inputData)` to `table.body.createViewData(inputData)` in `MainContainer.mjs` and `MainContainer2.mjs`, but `Neo.table.Body#createViewData()` (`src/table/Body.mjs:356-365`) takes no arguments and reads directly from `this.store.getCount()` / `this.store.getAt(i)`. Because the three example tables had `store: null`, `MainContainer3.mjs` would have thrown `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getCount')` as soon as the earlier containers stopped throwing. Giving each table `store: {model: {fields}}`, adding `id: i` to each generated row in `Viewport#createRandomData`, and loading rows through `table.store.data = inputData` across all three containers resolves both ACs cleanly without introducing debt. (Reviewed with the full template per `pr-review-guide.md §6.4` bounded-repair guard because the repair legitimately touches `MainContainer3.mjs`, `Viewport.mjs`, and `examples/tablePerformance/fields.mjs` beyond the two files named in `#19934`'s initial prescription.)

**Peer-Review Opening:** Thank you, @bercedev — specifically for running `examples/tablePerformance` in headless Chromium, catching that `#19934`'s suggested `table.body.createViewData(inputData)` call fails on `store.getCount()` when `table.store` is `null`, and migrating all three tables to `store: {model: {fields}}` and `table.store.data = inputData` so the initial render and the refresh controls work end-to-end. ### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** Ticket `#19934`, `examples/tablePerformance/Viewport.mjs`, `examples/tablePerformance/MainContainer.mjs`, `examples/tablePerformance/MainContainer3.mjs`, `src/table/Container.mjs`, `src/table/Body.mjs`, and `src/data/Model.mjs`.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** `Neo.table.Body#createViewData()` (`src/table/Body.mjs:356-365`) builds rows from `this.store` (`store.getCount()`, `store.getAt(i)`), and `applyRendererOutput` (`src/table/Body.mjs:156-167`) + `columnDefaults.renderer` (`MainContainer.mjs:80-87`) read `record[dataField]` and `record[dataField + 'style']`. Therefore each `TableContainer` in `examples/tablePerformance/` needs an inline `store` with model fields covering `id`, `column0`..`column9`, and `column0style`..`column9style`, `Viewport#createRandomData` must supply a unique `id` key per row, and `updateTableViewData()` must assign `table.store.data = inputData` (which triggers `TableBody#onStoreLoad` -> `createViewData()`). It must not reintroduce store-less `createViewData(inputData)` arguments on `src/table/Body.mjs`.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches and improves upon the ticket's initial prescription — `examples/tablePerformance/fields.mjs` defines `{name: 'id', type: 'Integer'}` plus `column0`..`column9` and `column0style`..`column9style`, `Viewport#createRandomData` seeds `data.push({id: i})`, and `MainContainer.mjs`, `MainContainer2.mjs`, and `MainContainer3.mjs` configure `store: {model: {fields}}` and assign `table.store.data = inputData`.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with `verify-before-assert` — the author verified the ticket's suggested call in a real browser, diagnosed why `table.body.createViewData(inputData)` failed against `src/table/Body.mjs:356-359`, and fixed the root cause across all three containers.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: Non-blocking observation: `examples/tablePerformance/fields.mjs` generates field definitions for `i < 10` (`column0`..`column9`), while `MainContainer#updateTableViewData` passes `columns = table.headerToolbar.items.length` into `Viewport#createRandomData(columns, rows)`. Because all three example containers define exactly 10 columns (`column0`..`column9`), the schema matches; if a future edit adds an 11th column to one of the containers, `fields.mjs` would need its loop bound bumped to match. I also verified in `src/data/Model.mjs:52-56,158-189` that sharing the exported `fields` array across all three `store: {model: {fields}}` declarations is safe because `Model#updateFieldsMap` reads field descriptors into each model instance's own `this.fieldsMap` without mutating the input array in place.
